about: THE TRADING YEAR BY REGION (Design/research_trade_seasons_and_hints.md, section 2, as data; edit freely). For each trade region of goods_793.json and each month (1 January to 12 December): 'comes': the goods that come to its markets that month (plenty, and cheap); 'wanted': the goods it wants that month (dear); 'fairs': the fairs, markets and things that draw buyers; 'feasts': the feasts kept; 'closed': why no ship gets there that month (empty: the water is open); 'line': the month in one plain line, shown on the port's card on the map. The word on an item (Known.Word, rule 5, the season) reads 'wanted' and 'comes' for the port's region and month; with neither it falls back on the good's own dear and cheap months in goods_793.json. NOTHING HERE MOVES A PRICE: prices follow goods_793.json (made, wanted, cheap, dear) and seasons_793.json. So that the word never lies, every good under 'comes' is one the region makes in goods_793.json and never in one of its dear months, and every good under 'wanted' is one the region wants there and never in one of its cheap months (the tests check it). Items from the sources are plain; inferences are marked (guess). The fairs' months match fairs_793.json. The lines are placeholders for your words.

rhine_delta.name: The Rhine delta: Dorestad, Utrecht
rhine_delta.note: The player's home. The riverbank toll of 777 and the mint all year. The river is closed only in the chronicle's hard winters (810/11, 813/14, 821/22, 859/60).

1.line: The river is quiet. Fish is wanted for the fast to come; the wine is still cheap.

2.line: Lent begins: herring and stockfish sell. The Rhine runs high and little comes down (guess).

3.line: The first boats move. Iron and the winter's stock go out; cattle are dear.

4.line: Easter: the sailing season opens and the Frisians cross to England.

fairs: The king's assembly: his men buy horses and gifts (guess)
5.line: The king's men come to buy (guess). The fleets are out.

6.line: Long days, light winds. The old wine is running low and dear.

7.line: The best sailing. Wine is dearest now; timber is wanted for the ships.

8.line: Harvest upstream. The quays are full of foreign ships.

9.line: The northern cargo comes south. The vintage starts on the Rhine.

10.line: The new wine comes down the Rhine, and cheap.

11.line: Martinmas: the new wine is in. The slaughter; the sea closes for most.

12.line: Christmas. The ships are hauled up; the wine is cheap.

zeeland.name: The Scheldt and Maas mouths: Walcheren
zeeland.note: Walcheren is in Danish hands from 841 (Harald's grant): the toll becomes a gift in kind.

1.line: Storms on the shoals. Little moves.

2.line: Lent. The salt pans lie under water.

3.line: The first Rhine boats bring pottery.

4.line: Easter. Salt is running low and dear.

5.line: The sheep are out on the salt marsh. Salt is dear.

6.line: The pans are dug and the peat is cut. Salt is dearest.

7.line: The salt making is on. Cheese comes to market.

8.line: Cheese is plentiful. Ships want timber for repairs.

9.line: The new salt is ready, and cheap.

10.line: Salt is cheap; the madder is dug (guess).

11.line: The slaughter: everyone wants salt, and here it is cheap.

12.line: Christmas. Gales and floods on the islands.

frisia.name: Frisia: the mound country from West Frisia to the Ems
frisia.note: The Frisians are above all carriers: the ships and the men. A ship makes two England runs a season (guess): over on the spring easterlies, home on the westerlies.

1.line: The looms are busy in every house. Butter is dear.

2.line: The ships are tarred and mended: tar and iron are wanted.

3.line: The new cloth is ready. Grain is running out on the mounds.

4.line: The spring easterlies: the ships cross to England with cloth.

5.line: The hungry gap: grain is dear. The cattle go out to the marsh.

6.line: Shearing: the new wool. Butter is at its best.

7.line: Cheese and butter are plentiful. Timber is wanted, as ever.

8.line: The ships come home on the westerlies. Cheese is cheap.

9.line: The eel runs begin. Cattle are driven to market.

10.line: Cattle and oxen are sold. Amber is gathered after the gales.

11.line: The slaughter: hides and horn are plentiful.

12.line: Christmas. The ships are hauled up and the looms start again.

rhineland.name: The Rhineland: Cologne, Mainz, the Eifel's Mayen
rhineland.note: The Frankfurt price caps of 794; the famine rules of Thionville (805) and Nijmegen (806); the Rhine frozen for thirty days in 821/22.

1.line: The pressed wine rests in the casks. Wax is wanted for Candlemas.

2.line: Lent: fish from the coast sells. The potters and stone cutters build their stock.

3.line: The river opens: querns, pots and glass go down to the delta.

4.line: Easter: every church wants wine and wax. The boats are busy.

5.line: The roads dry. The king holds his assembly (guess).

6.line: The old wine runs low. Pepper and silk come up from the south.

7.line: Hay, and the hungry weeks: grain is dear until the harvest.

8.line: Harvest: grain is cheap. The towing paths are busy.

9.line: The vintage begins south of Mainz.

10.line: The new wine is pressed and racked.

11.line: Martinmas: the new wine goes down the river, cheap. Furs are wanted for the winter.

12.line: Christmas. Ice on the river in a hard year.

meuse.name: The Meuse valley: Maastricht, Huy, Dinant

1.line: The founders work at Huy and Dinant. The river is high.

2.line: Lent. Little moves on the river.

3.line: The boats start down to the delta.

4.line: Easter. Brass goes down river on the spring water.

5.line: The brass founders sell to the Rhine and the coast.

6.line: Low water begins: the boats load light.

7.line: Hay; grain is dear before the harvest.

8.line: Harvest: wheat is cheap.

9.line: The grain goes down to the delta.

10.line: The autumn rains bring the water back.

11.line: Martinmas. The slaughter.

12.line: Christmas. The river runs high and brown.

1.line: The weavers want wool, and it is dear.

2.line: Lent: fish sells. The looms are busy.

3.line: The winter's cloth is ready.

4.line: Easter. Cloth goes to market; linen is bleached on the grass.

5.line: The sheep are washed for shearing.

6.line: Shearing. The old wine is dear.

7.line: The flax is pulled.

8.line: Harvest: wheat is cheap.

9.line: The flax is retted in the ditches.

10.line: The pigs are in the woods for the mast.

11.line: The slaughter: salt pork is laid down. The dyers want woad and madder.

neustria.name: Neustria: Paris and Saint-Denis, the Seine, Rouen, Quentovic
neustria.note: The breadbasket. Quentovic's mint and its tenth. The Channel short crossing runs most of the year; the Seine froze in 821/22.

1.line: The abbeys' granaries are still full. Wax is wanted for Candlemas.

fairs: The fair of Saint Mathias at Saint-Denis (24 Feb)
2.line: Lent, and the fair of Saint Mathias at Saint-Denis.

3.line: Lent: salt fish sells at every abbey gate.

4.line: Easter: wine for every church. The Channel crossing is busy again.

5.line: The king's men buy horses and hawks (guess).

6.line: Old wine is dear. The hay is cut along the Seine.

7.line: The hungry weeks before the harvest.

8.line: Harvest in the breadbasket: grain is cheap.

9.line: The vintage on the Seine begins.

fairs: The fair of Saint-Denis (from 9 Oct): Frisians and Saxons sell wool and cloth, and buy wine and honey
10.line: The fair of Saint-Denis opens on the ninth: wine and honey for wool and cloth.

fairs: The fair of Saint-Denis (from 9 Oct): Frisians and Saxons sell wool and cloth, and buy wine and honey
11.line: The fair runs on. The new wine is cheap; furs are wanted.

12.line: Christmas. Salmon and furs for the great halls.

loire.name: The Loire and the Bay: Nantes, Noirmoutier's salt
loire.note: The Noirmoutier monks fled the Northmen every summer from 819 and left for good in 836. The Irish wine trade starts here.

1.line: Winter gales in the Bay. The salt pans lie flooded.

2.line: Lent. The pans are cleaned out.

3.line: The first ships come for last year's salt.

4.line: Easter. Salt is running low and dear.

5.line: The pans are filled as the sun grows.

6.line: The salt making begins. Old wine is dear.

7.line: The salt is raked in the heat. Salt is still dear.

8.line: The new salt is heaped on the shore.

9.line: The salt ships load at Noirmoutier. The vintage begins.

10.line: Salt is cheap. The new wine is pressed.

11.line: The slaughter everywhere: the last salt ships sail. Wine is cheap.

1.line: The wine rests. Few ships cross the Bay in winter.

2.line: Lent. The vines are pruned.

3.line: The first ships for Ireland and Britain load wine.

4.line: Easter. Wine goes north for the churches.

5.line: The vines are in leaf. The sea road is open.

6.line: The old wine runs low and dear.

7.line: The heat. Little wine is left to sell.

8.line: The casks are made ready for the vintage.

9.line: The vintage begins on the Garonne.

10.line: The new wine is pressed, and cheap.

11.line: The wine ships sail for Ireland before the gales.

12.line: Christmas. The Bay is shut by storms.

saxony.name: Saxony: Westphalia, Engern, Eastphalia
saxony.note: The Saxon wars last until 804: a newly baptised country, whose new churches want everything.

1.line: Oak is felled in the frost and sledged to the rivers.

2.line: Lent in a newly baptised land. Timber is cheap.

3.line: The rafts go down the Weser and the Ems. The new churches want books.

4.line: Easter: the missions want relics, books and incense.

5.line: The king's army may be on the march (guess): the roads are not safe.

6.line: Midsummer. Honey is dear until the hives are taken.

7.line: Hay. The rye stands ripe.

8.line: Harvest: rye is cheap. The hives are taken: honey and wax.

9.line: Cattle are driven west to market. Nuts are gathered.

10.line: The pigs fatten in the oak woods. Salt is wanted.

11.line: The slaughter: salt pork and hides in plenty.

12.line: Christmas. The first hard frosts open the woods for felling.

england_south.name: Southern England: London, Hamwic, Kent
england_south.note: London's tolls are taken by the ship (c. 1000). The Danegeld years drain the silver (991, 994, 1002, 1007, 1012, 1018).

1.line: The weavers want wool; the minsters want wax for Candlemas.

2.line: Lent. The cloaks are finished for the spring ships.

3.line: The Frisians come over on the easterlies. Cloth goes to market.

4.line: Easter: every minster and hall wants wine.

5.line: The Channel is busy. Lead comes down from the Mendips (guess).

6.line: Shearing: the new wool is cheap. Old wine is dear.

7.line: Wine is dearest now. Wool is plentiful.

8.line: Harvest: grain is cheap, and the black stones are wanted to grind it.

9.line: The Frisians go home on the westerlies, laden with wool.

10.line: The last ships cross before the gales. The new wine is on its way.

11.line: The slaughter. The new wine comes over, and cheap.

12.line: Christmas: the halls feast. Furs and glass are wanted.

england_east.name: East Anglia and the Fens: Ipswich

1.line: The fens are flooded and frozen. Dried fish is wanted.

2.line: Lent: last autumn's herring is nearly gone, and dear.

3.line: The boats are tarred. The winter's cloth goes to market.

4.line: Easter. The potters at Ipswich fire their kilns again (guess).

5.line: Pots go up every river. The sheep are washed.

6.line: Shearing: wool is cheap here.

7.line: Hay: whetstones are wanted for the scythes. Wine is dear.

8.line: Harvest: barley is cheap. Querns are wanted.

9.line: The herring shoals come down the coast. The eel runs begin.

10.line: Herring is salted by the boatload, and cheap.

11.line: The fen eels are taken in their thousands. The slaughter.

12.line: Christmas. The malt is brewed for the feast.

northumbria.name: Northumbria: York, Lindisfarne, Whitby
northumbria.note: After 866 the Danish York wants the Norse goods too: soapstone, whetstones, furs, and ties to Dublin.

1.line: Snow on the moors. The monks want wax and oil for the long nights.

2.line: Lent at Lindisfarne and Jarrow.

3.line: The scribes want pigments as the light comes back.

4.line: Easter. Jet is gathered under the cliffs at Whitby after the winter (guess).

5.line: The first ships from Frisia reach the Humber.

6.line: Shearing. The salmon run in the Tyne and the Tweed.

7.line: Salmon is cheap. Wine is dear.

8.line: Harvest in the vale of York.

9.line: Oats and barley are cheap. The autumn gales begin.

10.line: Salt is wanted for the winter's meat.

11.line: The slaughter. Few ships come this far north now.

12.line: Christmas. The coast is shut by gales.

1.line: The salt houses at Droitwich boil on through the winter.

2.line: Lent. The pack roads are mud.

3.line: The salt ways open as the roads dry.

4.line: Easter. Pack horses carry salt to every shire.

5.line: Lead is dug in the hills (guess).

6.line: The brine is boiled day and night.

7.line: Salt is stacked for the autumn.

8.line: Harvest. Lead goes down the Severn.

9.line: Carts come from every shire for salt.

10.line: Salt is carried off for the slaughter.

11.line: The slaughter: the salt houses are emptied.

12.line: Christmas. The Dee and the Severn run high.

1.closed: Winter gales on a hard coast: no ship rounds the Lizard (guess).
1.line: Gales. The tin streams run too full to work.

2.closed: Winter gales on a hard coast: no ship rounds the Lizard (guess).
2.line: Winter still. Nobody comes.

3.line: The first ships dare the Lizard.

4.line: The tin streamers go back to the moors.

5.line: Tin is washed from the streams (guess).

6.line: Tin is smelted and run into blocks.

7.line: Ships from the Loire and Hamwic come for tin.

8.line: The best of the tin trade.

9.line: The last tin ships load before the gales.

10.line: The streams rise. The work stops.

11.line: Storms. The coast is empty.

12.closed: Winter gales on a hard coast: no ship rounds the Lizard (guess).

1.line: Yew is cut in the hills while the sap is down (guess).

2.line: Staves are split and stacked to season.

3.line: The staves are carried down to the coast.

4.line: Easter. The bowyers sell their winter's work.

5.line: The cattle go up to the summer dwellings.

6.line: Midsummer. The princes ride between their halls.

7.line: Hay on the hill farms.

8.line: A thin harvest of oats.

9.line: The cattle come down from the hills.

10.line: Salt is wanted before the slaughter.

11.line: The slaughter.

12.line: Midwinter. The princes feast in their halls.

ireland.name: Ireland
ireland.note: Dublin from 841: captives are traded northwards (871: two hundred ships of captives).

1.line: The kings keep to their halls. Salmon is dear.

feasts: Saint Brigid (1 Feb): the first milk
2.line: Saint Brigid's day: the first milk. Lent begins.

3.line: Lent. The monasteries want pigments for their books.

4.line: Easter. Salt is dear; the wine ships are awaited.

feasts: Beltaine (1 May): the cattle go to the summer pastures
5.line: Beltaine: the cattle go to the summer pastures.

6.line: Butter is at its best. The salmon run.

7.line: The wine ships from the Loire and Bordeaux come in. Wine is dear.

fairs: The fair of Tailtiu at Lughnasa (early August)
8.line: Lughnasa: the fair of Tailtiu. The oats are cut.

9.line: The cattle come back from the hills. Captives come to market after the summer.

10.line: Cattle are counted and sold: they are the wealth here.

11.line: Samain: the slaughter. Hides in plenty.

12.line: Christmas. Storms shut the western sea.

dalriata.name: Dal Riata and the Isles: Iona

1.closed: Winter storms cut the isles off (guess).
1.line: Winter in the isles. Otters are trapped for their winter coats.

feasts: Saint Brigid (1 Feb): the first milk
2.closed: Winter storms cut the isles off (guess).
2.line: Lent on Iona.

3.line: Gales still. The fish is hung to dry (guess).

4.line: Easter. The first skin boats cross from Ireland.

feasts: Beltaine (1 May): the cattle go to the summer pastures
5.line: The sea road between Ireland and the isles is open.

6.line: The salmon run. Dried fish comes to market.

7.line: The wine ships reach Iona, if they come at all. Wine is dear.

8.line: The oats are cut.

9.line: Oats are cheap. The autumn gales begin.

10.line: The boats are drawn up.

11.line: Samain. Otter pelts are at their best.

12.closed: Winter storms cut the isles off (guess).

shetland.name: Shetland and Orkney
shetland.note: Pictish and Christian in 793; Norse from about 800.

feasts: Midwinter: the Yule ale and the midwinter sacrifice (a guess at the day)
1.closed: The northern sea is shut by gales and the dark.
1.line: Dark and storm. No ship comes.

2.closed: The northern sea is shut by gales and the dark.
2.line: Storms still.

3.closed: The northern sea is shut by gales and the dark.
3.line: The days lengthen. The sea is still too wild.

feasts: The sacrifice at the start of summer (guess)
4.line: The first ships from Norway may come west.

5.line: Soapstone is cut from the rock face (guess).

6.line: Light all night. Ships pass on their way west and south.

7.line: The stone bowls are carved and sold to passing ships.

8.line: The last of the summer's ships. Fish is dried on the stones.

9.line: The gales begin. The ships go home.

10.line: The boats are drawn up.

11.closed: The northern sea is shut by gales and the dark.
11.line: The sea is shut.

12.closed: The northern sea is shut by gales and the dark.

jutland.name: Jutland: Ribe
jutland.note: Ribe is a summer market in the 8th century (booths and workshops, no houses), a town later. The king's man takes his due in gifts.

feasts: Midwinter: the Yule ale and the midwinter sacrifice (a guess at the day)
1.closed: Ice in the shallows and winter gales: no ship comes (guess).
1.line: Midwinter. The comb makers want antler.

2.closed: Ice in the shallows and winter gales: no ship comes (guess).
2.line: Ice on the shallows. The halls live on their stores.

3.line: The ships are tarred. The chieftains want swords before the season (guess).

feasts: The sacrifice at the start of summer (guess)
4.line: The sea opens. Shed antler is gathered in the woods.

fairs: The summer market at Ribe: bead makers, comb makers and bronze casters in their booths
5.line: The summer market opens at Ribe: the bead makers want glass.

fairs: The summer market at Ribe: bead makers, comb makers and bronze casters in their booths
6.line: The market is full: beads, combs, brooches. Wine is dear.

fairs: The summer market at Ribe: bead makers, comb makers and bronze casters in their booths
7.line: The Frisians bring pots, querns and wine. The best of the market.

fairs: The summer market at Ribe: bead makers, comb makers and bronze casters in their booths
8.line: Harvest: rye and barley. Querns are wanted.

9.line: The market is over. Cattle are driven down the ox road.

10.line: Winter nights. Amber is gathered after the gales.

11.line: The ships are hauled up. Amber is cheap.

12.line: Yule. The booths at Ribe stand empty.

schleswig.name: Schleswig: Sliesthorp (Hedeby)
schleswig.note: The hub between the Baltic and the west: the portage at Hollingstedt (under 15 km) saves the passage round Skagen. Ibrahim ibn Yaqub (960s) saw a feast with sacrifice here.

feasts: Midwinter: the Yule ale and the midwinter sacrifice (a guess at the day)
1.closed: The Schlei is frozen (guess).
1.line: Ice on the Schlei. The craftsmen want antler.

2.closed: The Schlei is frozen (guess).
2.line: Still frozen. Sledges cross the fjord.

3.line: The ice breaks. The ships are made ready.

feasts: The sacrifice at the start of summer (guess)
4.line: The portage from the west opens: glass and brass are wanted.

5.line: The market fills from both seas.

fairs: The market at Sliesthorp: the portage from the west and the Baltic ships meet here
6.line: The Baltic ships are in. Wine is dear.

fairs: The market at Sliesthorp: the portage from the west and the Baltic ships meet here
7.line: The best of the trade between the two seas.

fairs: The market at Sliesthorp: the portage from the west and the Baltic ships meet here
8.line: The northern cargo arrives: whetstones, soapstone, furs.

9.line: The last Baltic crossings. The market thins.

10.line: Winter nights. The traders go home.

11.line: The ships are hauled up along the fjord.

12.closed: The Schlei is frozen (guess).
12.line: Yule. Feasting and sacrifice (guess at the month).

feasts: Midwinter: the Yule ale and the midwinter sacrifice (a guess at the day)
1.closed: Ice in the Belts in a hard winter (guess).
1.line: Midwinter at Lejre: the king feasts his men.

2.closed: Ice in the Belts in a hard winter (guess).
2.line: Ice in the Belts. Herring is nearly gone, and dear.

3.line: The king's men fit out. Swords are wanted.

feasts: The sacrifice at the start of summer (guess)
4.line: The summer sacrifice. The ships are launched.

5.line: The fleets are out. Horses are wanted for the king's men.

6.line: Midsummer. Butter is plentiful.

7.line: The halls are half empty: the men are at sea.

8.line: Harvest: barley is cheap. Querns are wanted.

9.line: The herring come into the Sound.

10.line: Herring is salted in every bay, and cheap. The ships come home.

11.line: The ships are hauled up.

feasts: Midwinter: the Yule ale and the midwinter sacrifice (a guess at the day)
1.closed: Ice along the Baltic shore (guess).
1.line: Ice along the shore.

2.closed: Ice along the Baltic shore (guess).
2.line: Still frozen. Herring is nearly gone.

3.line: The ice goes out.

feasts: The sacrifice at the start of summer (guess)
4.line: The first ships come up the river to Ahus.

5.line: The craftsmen set up their booths at Ahus (guess).

6.line: Midsummer. A small market on the river.

7.line: Ships pass between the Sound and the east.

8.line: Harvest.

9.line: The herring come to the coast.

10.line: Herring is salted, and cheap.

11.line: The last ships pass. The boats are drawn up.

wendland.name: The Wends: the Obodrites' Reric
wendland.note: Reric was destroyed by Godfred in 808 and its merchants moved to Sliesthorp.

1.closed: Ice along the south shore of the Baltic.
1.line: Ice on the bays. Furs are trapped in the woods.

2.closed: Ice along the south shore of the Baltic.
2.line: Still frozen.

3.closed: Ice along the south shore of the Baltic.
3.line: The ice goes out. The winter's furs come to market.

4.line: The ships come: swords and mail are wanted, law or no law.

5.line: Furs are cheap. The Danes come to trade, and to take.

6.line: Midsummer. Honey is dear until the hives are cut.

7.line: The border is restless (guess).

8.line: Harvest. The wild hives are cut: honey and wax.

prussia.name: The Prussians: Truso, the amber coast
prussia.note: Wulfstan: seven days and nights under sail from Hedeby to Truso. No salt is made here.

1.closed: The lagoon at Truso is frozen.
1.line: The lagoon is frozen. Amber is picked from the winter beaches.

2.line: Frozen still. Sledges carry the amber inland.

3.line: The ice begins to break.

4.line: The first ships from Hedeby are awaited. Salt is dear.

6.line: Midsummer. Salt is dearest; none is made here.

7.line: The amber workers sell beads to the ships.

8.line: The hives are cut: honey and wax.

9.line: Honey and wax are cheap. Captives are sold.

10.line: The autumn gales throw amber on the beaches.

2.closed: The eastern Baltic is frozen.

vestfold.name: Vestfold and the Vik: Kaupang
vestfold.note: Ohthere: five days from Skiringssal to Hedeby. The Klastad ship (c. 990) sank with a cargo of whetstones. The market may have stayed a summer one.

feasts: Midwinter: the Yule ale and the midwinter sacrifice (a guess at the day)
1.closed: The head of the Vik is frozen and the ships are hauled up (guess).
1.line: Midwinter. Oak and pine are felled and dragged on the snow.

2.closed: The head of the Vik is frozen and the ships are hauled up (guess).
2.line: Iron is smelted from the bog ore. Timber is cheap.

3.closed: The head of the Vik is frozen and the ships are hauled up (guess).
3.line: Grain is running short. The ships are tarred and rigged.

feasts: The sacrifice at the start of summer (guess)
4.line: The ships are launched. Salt and grain are dear.

fairs: The summer market at Skiringssal (Kaupang)
5.line: The market opens at Skiringssal. Iron comes down from the valleys.

fairs: The summer market at Skiringssal (Kaupang)
6.line: Whetstones from Eidsborg and soapstone pots fill the booths.

fairs: The summer market at Skiringssal (Kaupang)
7.line: The best of the market: Frisians, Danes and men from the north. Wine is dear.

8.line: The northern cargo passes south: furs, walrus rope, down.

9.line: The last ships sail for Hedeby.

10.line: Winter nights: the ships are hauled up.

11.line: The halls live on their stores.

12.closed: The head of the Vik is frozen and the ships are hauled up (guess).

norway_west.name: Western Norway: Avaldsnes, Hordaland
norway_west.note: Grain is wanted here in every bad year. Stockfish goes south only from about 1000.

feasts: Midwinter: the Yule ale and the midwinter sacrifice (a guess at the day)
1.closed: No ship crosses the North Sea in winter.
1.line: Midwinter. Timber is felled; the looms are busy.

2.closed: No ship crosses the North Sea in winter.
2.line: Masts are dragged to the fjords on the snow.

3.closed: No ship crosses the North Sea in winter.
3.line: Grain is running out. The new wadmal and sailcloth are ready.

feasts: The sacrifice at the start of summer (guess)
4.line: The ships are launched. Grain and salt are dear.

5.line: The men sail west and south. Soapstone is quarried.

fairs: The Gulathing meets (from about 900)
6.line: The Gulathing meets. Down is gathered; butter is at its best.

7.line: Salmon and butter are cheap. Wine is dear, when there is any.

8.line: The northern ships pass south with their cargo.

9.line: Falcons are taken on the cliffs. The ships come home.

10.line: Winter nights: the ships are hauled up. Cloth is wanted for the winter.

11.closed: No ship crosses the North Sea in winter.
11.line: The fjords are quiet. The slaughter.

12.closed: No ship crosses the North Sea in winter.

norway_north.name: Halogaland and the Sami (Ohthere's country)
norway_north.note: Ohthere: the Sami tribute of marten, reindeer, bear and otter skins, feathers, and ship ropes of whale and seal hide. One could not sail to Skiringssal in a month, camping at night. Stockfish from about 1000.

feasts: Midwinter: the Yule ale and the midwinter sacrifice (a guess at the day)
1.closed: The northern coast is shut by the dark, ice and gales.
1.line: Dark all day. The cod come to Lofoten.

2.closed: The northern coast is shut by the dark, ice and gales.
2.line: The cod fishing. The Sami bring their tribute of furs.

3.closed: The northern coast is shut by the dark, ice and gales.
3.line: The fish hangs on the racks to dry. The furs are counted.

feasts: The sacrifice at the start of summer (guess)
4.line: The sun is back. The winter's furs and hides are ready to ship.

5.line: The ships leave for the south with furs and hides.

6.line: Light all night. The dried fish comes off the racks. Down is gathered.

7.line: The walrus hunt in the White Sea. Falcons are taken.

8.line: The hunters are home: walrus ivory and hide rope.

9.line: The last ships south. Cloth is wanted before the dark.

10.closed: The northern coast is shut by the dark, ice and gales.
10.line: The sea is shut. The Sami go to their winter grounds.

11.closed: The northern coast is shut by the dark, ice and gales.
11.line: Dark and storm.

12.closed: The northern coast is shut by the dark, ice and gales.

svealand.name: The Svear: Birka, Uppsala
svealand.note: Prime pelts are winter pelts. Birka's winter market, reached by sled and skate, is inferred; the Disting is attested late: both are the game's own dates. The one place to trade in winter.

fairs: The winter market at Birka, over the ice by sled and skate (inferred)
feasts: Midwinter: the Yule ale and the midwinter sacrifice (a guess at the day)
1.closed: The lake is frozen: no ship reaches Birka (a guess at the months), though sledges do.
1.line: The lake is frozen: the winter market at Birka, by sled and skate. Furs come in.

fairs: The winter market at Birka, over the ice by sled and skate (inferred)
The Disting at Uppsala: a thing and a market (attested later)
2.closed: The lake is frozen: no ship reaches Birka (a guess at the months), though sledges do.
2.line: The Disting at Uppsala: a thing, a market and a sacrifice. Iron is sold.

3.closed: The lake is frozen: no ship reaches Birka (a guess at the months), though sledges do.
3.line: The winter's furs are sorted. Still ice.

feasts: The sacrifice at the start of summer (guess)
4.line: The ice breaks on the lake. Grain and salt are dear.

5.line: The first ships reach Birka. Furs are cheap.

fairs: The summer market at Birka
6.line: The summer market: Frisian cloth, glass and wine are wanted.

fairs: The summer market at Birka
7.line: The best of the market. Silver from the east changes hands.

fairs: The summer market at Birka
8.line: The eastern ships are home from Ladoga with silk and silver.

9.line: The last ships leave for Hedeby.

10.line: Winter nights. The ships are hauled up.

11.line: The lake begins to freeze.

12.closed: The lake is frozen: no ship reaches Birka (a guess at the months), though sledges do.

gotland.name: Gotland
gotland.note: The Baltic's bank: farmers who are traders.

feasts: Midwinter: the Yule ale and the midwinter sacrifice (a guess at the day)
1.closed: Winter gales, and ice in the harbours (guess).
1.line: The farmers who are traders sit at home with their silver.

2.closed: Winter gales, and ice in the harbours (guess).
2.line: Winter still.

3.closed: Winter gales, and ice in the harbours (guess).
3.line: The ships are made ready.

feasts: The sacrifice at the start of summer (guess)
4.line: The Gotlanders sail east and south. Salt is dear.

5.line: Their ships are at Grobina, Truso and Ladoga.

6.line: Midsummer. Salt is dearest.

7.line: The island is the Baltic's meeting place.

8.line: Beads and silver come back from the east.

9.line: The ships come home.

10.line: Winter nights. Silver is buried for safe keeping.

11.line: The boats are drawn up.

12.closed: Winter gales, and ice in the harbours (guess).

ladoga.name: Ladoga: Aldeigjuborg, the gate to the east
ladoga.note: The dirham stream runs from about 800 to 1015, at its height 900-950. Ibn Fadlan (922): the Rus pray for a merchant with many dinars and dirhams.

1.closed: Ladoga and the Volkhov are frozen: the ice breaks in April or May.
1.line: Frozen. The furs come in by sled from the forests.

2.closed: Ladoga and the Volkhov are frozen: the ice breaks in April or May.
2.line: Frozen. The best pelts of the year.

3.closed: Ladoga and the Volkhov are frozen: the ice breaks in April or May.
3.line: The winter's furs are sorted and baled.

4.closed: Ladoga and the Volkhov are frozen: the ice breaks in April or May.
4.line: The ice still holds. Grain and salt are dear.

5.line: The floods open the rivers. Furs are cheap.

fairs: The river convoys leave for the south (the Dnieper convoys leave Kiev in June)
6.line: The ships from the west arrive: swords, cloth and beads are wanted. The convoys go south.

7.line: Silver and silk come up the rivers from the east.

8.line: The hives are cut. The western ships load furs and wax.

9.line: The last ships leave for the Baltic.

10.line: The first ice on the Volkhov.

11.closed: Ladoga and the Volkhov are frozen: the ice breaks in April or May.
11.line: The lake shore freezes.

12.closed: Ladoga and the Volkhov are frozen: the ice breaks in April or May.

rus_volga.name: The Volga: the Bulgars, the furs of the north east

1.closed: The Volga is frozen.
1.line: The river is ice. Sable is trapped in the northern forests.

2.closed: The Volga is frozen.
2.line: Frozen.

3.line: The winter's sable comes down by sled.

4.line: The ice breaks; the floods run.

5.line: The river opens. The Rus come down with furs and captives.

6.line: The market of the Bulgars: furs for silver.

7.line: Captives and furs go on down the river.

8.line: Wax and honey. The traders start back north.

9.line: The last boats go upriver.

10.line: The first ice.

11.line: Frozen.

12.closed: The Volga is frozen.

khazaria.name: The Khazars: Itil
khazaria.note: The Khazars take a tenth on the river trade.

1.closed: The lower Volga is frozen.
1.line: The lower river is frozen. The khagan winters in his city.

2.closed: The lower Volga is frozen.
2.line: Frozen.

3.line: The ice goes out.

4.line: The Khazars go out to the summer pastures.

5.line: The river trade begins. The tenth is taken on every boat.

6.line: The Rus arrive with furs and captives.

7.line: The caravans come in from the east.

8.line: The best of the market at Itil.

9.line: The traders start for home.

10.line: The Khazars come back to the city.

11.line: The first ice.

12.closed: The lower Volga is frozen.

caliphate.name: The Caliphate: Baghdad, Egypt, Persia
caliphate.note: Its feasts follow the moon's year and move through the seasons, so none is fixed to a month here. News from here is months old in the north.

1.line: Winter in Baghdad: furs are worn at court.

2.line: The caravans rest.

3.line: The spring caravans set out. Falcons are wanted.

4.line: The ships from India come in on the monsoon (guess): pepper and cinnamon.

5.line: Spices are plentiful. The caravans cross to the Caspian.

6.line: The heat begins. Amber is prized.

7.line: The northern traders reach the Caspian with furs and captives.

8.line: The slave markets are full.

9.line: The dates are picked.

10.line: The cold comes: furs are wanted, and dear.

11.line: Sable is worth its weight. The cane is cut (guess).

byzantium.name: Byzantium: Constantinople
byzantium.note: The treaty of 944 caps the silk a Rus may buy at 50 gold coins a man. Constantine VII: the Dnieper convoys leave Kiev in June.

1.closed: The sea is closed to ships for the winter.
1.line: The sea is closed. The city lives behind its walls.

2.closed: The sea is closed to ships for the winter.
2.line: Closed still.

3.line: Lent. The sea opens again. Falcons are wanted.

4.line: Easter in the Great Church.

5.line: The spice ships come up from Egypt and Syria.

6.line: The Rus set out down the Dnieper with furs and captives.

7.line: The Rus arrive: they may buy silk, but only so much a man.

8.line: The best of the market. Amber is prized.

9.line: The Rus start home before the rivers freeze.

10.line: The cold comes: furs are wanted at court.

11.closed: The sea is closed to ships for the winter.
11.line: The sea closes.

12.closed: The sea is closed to ships for the winter.

1.closed: The Alpine passes are under snow and the sea is closed.
1.line: The olives are pressed: oil is cheap. The passes are shut.

2.closed: The Alpine passes are under snow and the sea is closed.
2.line: Lent in Rome.

3.line: The sea opens. Pilgrims set out for Easter.

4.line: Easter in Rome: the pilgrims come, and go home with relics.

5.line: The passes open: oil, spices and relics go north.

6.line: The Venetians bring spice and silk from the east.

7.line: Coral is fished off the southern coasts.

8.line: The almond harvest. The heat.

9.line: Figs are dried. The grape harvest.

10.line: The last travellers cross the Alps before the snow.

11.line: The olive harvest begins. The passes close.

12.closed: The Alpine passes are under snow and the sea is closed.

spain.name: Al-Andalus: Cordoba
spain.note: Pagan Slavs are sold lawfully through Verdun to Spain. Its feasts follow the moon's year.

1.line: The olives are pressed: oil is cheap.

2.line: The almond trees flower.

3.line: The sea opens to the ships of the coast.

4.line: The emir's army musters for the summer raid north (guess).

5.line: Kermes is gathered from the oaks for the red dye.

6.line: The slave traders come down from Verdun (guess).

7.line: The heat. Captives are wanted in Cordoba.

8.line: The almond harvest.

9.line: Rice and cotton are harvested.

10.line: The harvests are sold.

11.line: The olive harvest begins; the cane is cut.

provence.name: Provence and the Rhone: Marseille, Arles
provence.note: Saracen pirates hold the coast from the 840s.

1.closed: The sea is closed for the winter.
1.line: The olives are pressed: oil is cheap.

2.closed: The sea is closed for the winter.
2.line: Lent. The mistral blows.

3.line: The sea opens. Boats go up the Rhone again.

4.line: Easter. Oil goes north for the church lamps.

5.line: Kermes is gathered for the red dye.

6.line: Ships from the east put in at Marseille: spice, silk, papyrus.

7.line: Coral is fished along the coast.

8.line: The almond harvest.

9.line: The grape harvest. The eastern goods go up the Rhone.

10.line: The last ships of the year.

11.line: The olive harvest begins. The sea closes.

12.closed: The sea is closed for the winter.

iceland.name: Iceland (settled from 874)
iceland.note: Before 874 only birds and a few Irish hermits. The Althing from 930; Christian from 1000.

feasts: Midwinter: the Yule ale and the midwinter sacrifice (a guess at the day)
1.closed: No ship crosses to Iceland in winter.
1.line: Dark and snow. Wadmal is woven in every house.

2.closed: No ship crosses to Iceland in winter.
2.line: Winter still. The foxes are trapped.

3.closed: No ship crosses to Iceland in winter.
3.line: The stores run low.

feasts: The sacrifice at the start of summer (guess)
4.closed: No ship crosses to Iceland in winter.
4.line: The sea is still shut.

5.line: The first ships are looked for.

fairs: The Althing meets at the end of June (from 930)
6.line: The Althing meets. The ships come from Norway: timber is wanted above all.

7.line: Wadmal, down and sulphur for timber, grain and iron.

8.line: Falcons are taken for kings. The best of the trade.

9.line: The ships leave before the gales.

10.closed: No ship crosses to Iceland in winter.
10.line: Winter nights. Nobody sails now.

11.closed: No ship crosses to Iceland in winter.
11.line: The sheep are brought in.

12.closed: No ship crosses to Iceland in winter.

greenland.name: Greenland (settled from 985)
greenland.note: Settled from 985. One ship in a summer is a good year.

feasts: Midwinter: the Yule ale and the midwinter sacrifice (a guess at the day)
1.closed: Ice shuts the fjords and no ship comes.
1.line: Ice and dark. The settlement lives on its stores.

2.closed: Ice shuts the fjords and no ship comes.
2.line: Winter.

3.closed: Ice shuts the fjords and no ship comes.
3.line: Seals are hunted on the ice.

feasts: The sacrifice at the start of summer (guess)
4.closed: Ice shuts the fjords and no ship comes.
4.line: The bears come down with the drift ice.

5.closed: Ice shuts the fjords and no ship comes.
5.line: The seal hunt. The fjords are still shut.

6.line: The ice loosens. The men row north to the hunting grounds.

7.line: A ship from Norway or Iceland may come: timber and iron are wanted.

8.line: The hunters come back with walrus ivory and hide rope.

9.line: The ship must leave before the ice.

10.closed: Ice shuts the fjords and no ship comes.
10.line: The fjords close.

11.closed: Ice shuts the fjords and no ship comes.
11.line: Winter.

12.closed: Ice shuts the fjords and no ship comes.
